editorial:
Thor gets locked up on the far side of the universe and must race home to stop Hela from destroying Asgard. Along the way, you meet a hilarious Hulk, a sneaky Loki, and a tough new hero named Valkyrie. The whole thing feels like a bright, colorful comic book come to life. Director Taika Waititi gives the movie a fun, lighthearted vibe that makes it stand out from darker superhero films. You will laugh a lot, but the stakes still feel real as Thor fights to save his people.

Chris Hemsworth shines as a funnier, more relaxed Thor, and Cate Blanchett is fantastic as the scary villain Hela. The action scenes are fast and exciting, especially the gladiator fight and the final battle. The pacing rarely slows down, so you stay hooked the whole time. On the downside, some jokes land better than others, and a few side characters do not get much screen time. Still, this is a great pick for Marvel fans and anyone who wants a fun movie night. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Thor realizes he cannot stop Ragnarok by fighting Hela alone. He sends Loki to free Surtur, the fire demon, who destroys Asgard completely. Hela is killed in the explosion. Thor escapes with the remaining Asgardians on a spaceship, becoming their new king. The twist is that Thor accepts Asgard is not a place but its people. The movie ends with Thor heading toward Earth, setting up future adventures.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves superhero movies with humor and big action.
